spans.s:
Ambarīṣa is mentioned as a vārṣāgira in the Rigveda along with ṛjrāśva, sahadeva, surādhas, and bhayamāna.
Foot notes i. 100, 17. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 140.

Āmba denotes in the taittirīya and kāṭhaka Saṃhitās a grain, called nāmba in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa
Foot notes i. 8, 10, 1.
xv. 5.
v. 3, 3, 8.

Āmbaṣṭhya is mentioned in the aitareya brāhmaṇa (viii. 21) as a king, whose priest for the rājasūya, or royal inauguration, was nārada. Presumably the name is local, meaning ‘King of the Ambaṣṭhas,’ as interpreted in the St. Petersburg Dictionary. Later the term ambaṣṭha denotes ‘a man of mingled brāhmaṇa and vaiśya parentage by father and mother’ respectively.
